state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's work through this together. Can you explain why you think Tom is correct and how you approached solving the problem?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I thought Tom was right because if you cut all the heights in half, the smallest and largest values would still be the same proportion apart, so the range wouldn't change. But now I'm not sure about Katie's idea. If they all grow by \(3 \mathrm{~cm}\), wouldn't that also change the smallest and largest values? How does that affect the range?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's focus on Katie's idea now. Think about how increasing each plant's height by \(3 \mathrm{~cm}\) would impact the overall spread of the heights. Can you see how this change would affect the range of the plant heights?
